name: Ojo Dibandingke
blurb: Abah Lala's Javanese dangdut hit that 12-year-old Farel Prayoga sang at Indonesia's palace
title: Ojo Dibandingke: The Javanese Song That Went Viral on TikTok
description: Ojo Dibandingke ("don't compare me") is a Javanese dangdut song by Abah Lala, already big on TikTok when child singer Farel Prayoga sang it at the palace.
answer: "Ojo Dibandingke" is a Javanese-language dangdut song written by Abah Lala (Agus Purwanto) from Boyolali, Central Java, and popularised by singer Denny Caknan in 2022. The title means "don't compare (me)". Already a TikTok favourite, it became the song of the year in Indonesia after 12-year-old Farel Prayoga sang it at Merdeka Palace in Jakarta on 17 August 2022, after the Independence Day ceremony, and guests got up to dance.

body: Farel Prayoga, a sixth-grader from Banyuwangi in East Java who had busked with his father after school, was invited to perform after the 77th Independence Day flag ceremony. His lively version set the audience of officials and guests dancing, and they called for an encore; he had prepared only one song, so he sang "Ojo Dibandingke" again. The broadcast was shown live, and clips spread across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube the same day.

body.note: Abah Lala watched on his phone and was filmed in tears of pride. He said the palace only called him about permission after the performance, and the next day he was handed the song's intellectual property certificate in Jakarta.

head: Date
Event
rows: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Abah Lala writes the song at a fried-chicken stall in Boyolali; it is first sung by Ndarboy Genk in Yogyakarta, then taken up by Denny Caknan.
The song trends on TikTok and keeps appearing on the For You page; by the day of the palace show, Farel's cover on YouTube has about 6.5 million views.
Farel sings it at Merdeka Palace after the Independence Day ceremony, and it peaks nationwide.
Abah Lala receives the song's intellectual property certificate from the Minister of Law and Human Rights.

body: In Javanese, "ojo" means "don't" and "dibandingke" means "be compared". The song is a heartbroken plea from someone who is being compared with a richer or better rival in love. Abah Lala has said it was inspired by a friend's real, sad story, in which his partner's family preferred another suitor.

ul: Dangdut rhythm: the drum-driven beat of Javanese dangdut makes people want to sway, which suits TikTok dance and joget clips.
A phrase everyone could use: "ojo dibandingke" became a jokey reply to anyone comparing you with siblings, exes or classmates.
The palace moment: a child singer making a formal state occasion dance was irresistible to share, and it turned Farel into a national celebrity.
Abah Lala was already known in dangdut circles for coining the "cendol dawet" crowd chant, so his name gave the story an extra hook.

faq.a: It was written by Abah Lala and is best known in versions by Denny Caknan and by child singer Farel Prayoga, whose palace performance on 17 August 2022 made it a national hit.
Javanese for "don't compare (me)". It is a plea not to be measured against someone else in love.
Javanese, the regional language of Central and East Java, sung in the dangdut style that is popular across Indonesia.
